es.summary: Etapa avanzada de la infección por VIH, cuando el sistema inmune está muy debilitado. En obstetricia lo central es detectar el VIH en el embarazo y prevenir la transmisión al bebé.
key_points: El SIDA se define por un conteo de CD4 menor de 200 células/µL o por una enfermedad definitoria de SIDA.
El VIH puede pasar al bebé durante el embarazo, el parto (sobre todo vaginal) y la lactancia materna.
La terapia antirretroviral (TAR) busca una carga viral indetectable: es lo que más protege al bebé.
Con carga viral alta (más de 1 000 copias/mL) se ofrece cesárea programada a las 38 semanas con zidovudina IV.
El RN recibe antirretrovirales lo antes posible después del nacer, durante 4 a 6 semanas.

usage: Se anota en antecedentes y diagnósticos: «G2P1, VIH positiva en TAR, carga viral indetectable».
VIH es el virus; SIDA es la etapa avanzada. No son sinónimos.
Las pruebas de VIH forman parte de los laboratorios del control prenatal.
nursing_care: Ofrecer la prueba de VIH lo antes posible en el embarazo, con consejería y confidencialidad.
Reforzar la toma diaria de la TAR: la adherencia es clave para la carga viral.
Aplicar precauciones estándar con todas las pacientes en el parto.
Seguir el protocolo institucional de alimentación del RN: donde hay fórmula segura, se indica en lugar de lactancia materna.
Coordinar el seguimiento del RN con pruebas de VIH en los primeros meses.

en.summary: Late-stage HIV infection, when the immune system is severely weakened (SIDA in Spanish). In obstetrics, the focus is testing for HIV in pregnancy and preventing transmission to the baby.
key_points: AIDS is defined as a CD4 count < 200 cells/microL or the presence of any AIDS-defining condition.
HIV can pass to the baby during pregnancy, during childbirth (especially vaginal birth) and during breastfeeding.
Antiretroviral therapy (ART) aims for an undetectable viral load, the best way to protect the baby.
With a viral load > 1,000 copies/mL, an elective C-section is offered at 38 weeks with intravenous zidovudine.
The baby gets HIV medicines as soon as possible after birth and takes them for 4 to 6 weeks.

usage: Charted in history and diagnoses: "G2P1, HIV positive on ART, undetectable viral load".
HIV is the virus; AIDS is the late stage. They are not synonyms.
HIV testing is part of the routine prenatal labs.
nursing_care: Offer HIV testing as early as possible in pregnancy, with counseling and confidentiality.
Reinforce taking ART every day: adherence is key to the viral load.
Use standard precautions with every patient during birth.
Follow the facility's infant feeding protocol: where safe formula is available, it is recommended instead of breastfeeding.
Coordinate the baby's follow-up with several HIV tests over the first months.

sources.name: MedlinePlus en español: VIH y el embarazo

key_points.0.quote: AIDS is defined as a CD4 count < 200 cells/microL or the presence of any AIDS-defining conditions, which include the following: bacterial infections, multiple or recurrent candidiasis of bronchi, trachea, or lungs candidiasis of esophagus cervical cancer, invasive coccidioidomycosis, disseminated or extrapulmonary cryptococcosis, extrapulmonary cryptosporidiosi

key_points.1.quote: It can happen in three ways: During pregnancy During childbirth, especially if it is vaginal childbirth During breastfeeding

key_points.2.quote: Having an undetectable viral load is the best thing you can do to stay healthy and prevent your baby from getting HIV.

key_points.3.quote: Patients with a viral load > 1,000 copies/mL should be offered an elective C-section at 38 weeks with intravenous zidovudine (Retrovir) given 3 hours preoperatively (ACOG, 2024).

key_points.4.quote: Your baby will need to take medicines for 4 to 6 weeks.

sections.usage.1.quote: Late-stage HIV is known as acquired immunodeficiency syndrome ( AIDS ) and is fatal (CDC, 2021a).

sections.usage.2.quote: Pregnant patients should be tested at the first prenatal visit and again in the third trimester.

sections.nursing_care.0.quote: If you are pregnant or planning to get pregnant, it's important to get tested for HIV as soon as possible.

sections.nursing_care.3.quote: So the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and the American Academy of Pediatrics recommend that if you have HIV, you should feed your baby formula instead of breastfeeding.

sections.nursing_care.4.quote: He or she will get several HIV tests over the first few months.
